title: Determinism and Chaos Theory
subtitle: A debate that has raged since the 19th century.

trails.title: Arrival and Departure
trails.description: They all look forward to the days ahead.

content.text: Seems you've got some iron beneath that calm surface.
Not everyone would sleep so soundly in a stranger's house.
Honestly, you could've just made yourself at home and stayed the night. When I take out the trash later, I'll be sure to toss you out along with it.

branch.text: Oh, spare me the details!
I'm sure it was full of enviable warmth and radiance—just enough to scorch my miserable, frozen heart.
Whatever you saw or did in that dream, do yourself a favor and let it go.
You did—and I owe you my thanks.
Your sleep talking added a bit of flavor to my otherwise bland meal.
I haven't had such an appealing appetizer in a long time.
What about my meal?
The soup's gone cold. That ship's sailed.
You may not like the reality served on your silver platter—no one does—but you'll have to swallow it.
Blame this mess on the black robes if you want; those cowards keep trying to drag the world back to their "good old days."
And the white robes preaching the future? No less clowns for their taste in uniforms—falling off their high horses again and again, brought down by their own arrogance.
Who would have thought? The whole universe turned into one circus starring two troupes of fools.
Why didn't that blind woman just let the world burn back then? It wouldn't have been worse than these chaotic times. And who asked her to play the martyr, anyway?
If you're lucky enough to find her, take her home—and make sure she stays there, quietly, for everyone's sake.

trails.title: Surprise Formula
trails.description: A cocktail no one can replicate. Every sip is a new adventure.

content.text: Give me a minute; I'll go deal with the intruder.
Walking into my home with blood-soaked boots! Tsk. Such insolence. Does he think sending people to die makes him special?
He'll pay for this in blood!

branch.text: That's nowhere near enough. He'll have to scrub every bloodstain off the floor.
I don't want to hear any excuses. This whole mess is his own fault.
I AM calm. He brought the blood here, so he'll pay by cleaning up every drop.
I won't even lend him a rag—he can use that fancy coat of his for all I care.
So he claims those "big shots" forced him to stain his hands, huh? How convenient.
And this plan to "restore everything to how it was"? Utterly foolish.
But the fact that he followed it to the letter makes him no different from the ones who devised it.
To realize their "grand vision," those so-called realists kept piling weight on one side of the scale ...
Sacrificing one innocent life after another just so someone could remember a name that wasn't hers anymore. Absurd.
I have one thing to say to those arrogant megalomaniacs wanting to play gods: anyone who has forgotten their own name is as good as dead—and forcing them to wear it again won't change a thing.
What happened has happened. Those bloody footprints can never truly be erased.

items.text: Carlota Bar
Sometime during the next day, a strange atmosphere hangs over the tavern where the gamblers usually gather.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: Mr. Tlazo ...

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Yeah?

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: That lucky-ass girl's been counting her winnings for a while now, along with some other girl.

items.speaker: Gang Grunt I
items.text: They planning something?

items.speaker: Gang Grunt II
items.text: Sir, you think it's time we—

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Cram it!
The rebuke comes like the snap of a frightened dog.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: We can't afford to mess with arcanists.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: Hers ain't no ordinary luck, I tell ya. Must've used some kinda witchcraft or somethin'.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: You heard about those people who drowned on dry land, or just up and disappeared from locked rooms? That's just the start of the weird s**t they get up to.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: One of our associates in the police told me that was all because of some arcane skill.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: So, unless you're lookin' to join those stiffs, you stay away from these outsiders.
As they trade wild theories about witchcraft and arcanum, the two figures in the corner exchange a glance over the opened letter in their hands.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: "When the sacred calendar and solar calendar realign, we celebrate the delaying of doomsday."

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: "We climb up the Hill of the Star and watch the stars reach their zenith."

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: "The annual art auction will commence soon. The Turquoise Serpent Club sincerely looks forward to your arrival."

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: Pft. Trying a little hard.

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: An art auction, huh? Ah, an invitation with no time or location!

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: So this is the letter of supposedly "incredible value"?

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: What's your excuse this time, Tlazo?

items.speaker: Centurion
items.text: It's gibberish. Do I have to remind you how much you owe me?
The eavesdropping capo straightens in his seat.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: I can't tell you nothin'. I mean it. I don't got a clue neither!

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: I got the thing off some desperate gambler. Claimed it holds the biggest secret in Mexico City.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: But before I could make him, ahem, I mean, ask him anythin' more, he skipped the border.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: As for this club, all I know is that it's hidden away in some plantation outside of the city. But I ain't never heard of no auction.

items.speaker: Gang Capo
items.text: No human's ever set foot in that place—arcanist territory.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Great. A conversation utterly devoid of useful information.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: This line on the invitation, "when the sacred and solar calendars realign," it's referring to an Aztec myth about the coming of the end of the world.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: So, once every 52 years, at the full cycle of the Aztec calendar, the Aztecs held their New Fire Ceremony to celebrate that they survived another cycle.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Before the new sun rose, they climbed up the Hill of the Star and watched the Pleiades star cluster reach its zenith.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Look at these symbols.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: These represent the 20 days in the Tonalpohualli.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Their order guides the flow of energy. It's an incantation to activate a ritual.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The key to its activation is the flint knife symbol, called the Tecpatl. It represents the date of the New Fire Ceremony.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The question is, where will the ritual take place?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: According to the changes observed in the Chaotic Energy within the area—

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: "A large-scale artificial supernatural phenomenon is likely to occur in Mexico."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: "Furthermore—and with no thanks to you brainless dolts—I was able to confirm my leads that pointed to Mexico City itself."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: "Imagine what you overboiled eggheads could do if you spent even a fraction of your time on something useful."
Conference Room, Laplace
In the meeting room, Ulrich tucks the letter away, his ferrofluid resting languid in his tank.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This is the latest update from Lorentz Butterfly.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: She's named the plan "The Nine Trials of Death."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Utterly ridiculous!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This is already the third letter from her this month! Are you seriously planning a joint paper with this Butterfly?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Naturally, and don't worry. I'll be sure to include your name in the acknowledgements.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Her first letter claimed that Lorentz's informants discovered a new type of arcane material, one that has been circulating across the globe since our reversal to 1920.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The Manus has been using it to revive the dead, smuggling the material under the guise of a common mineral pigment.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: In her second letter, she tracked down its source to Mexico City.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And now this! Some prophecy about a supernatural phenomenon!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The Butterfly's trying to provoke us, mocking us for always being a step behind Lorentz.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Do I have to remind you that she did the same thing after the third, sixth, and the seventh "Storms," Substitute Director Adler?

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Pardon my interruption, but you didn't call this meeting just for us to be an audience to your squabbling, did you?
Hearing the argument go on long enough, the focused researcher finally speaks up.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Certainly not.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Which reminds me, Pointer, I have something to tell you.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: In accordance with Plesetsk branch tradition, we have decided to hold a party to celebrate your and Hissabeth's successful completion of your field mission here at headquarters.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Though I personally disagree with the principle.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: In order to spare time for the party, I've informed the "Storm" Research Group to extend their workday to 12 hours for the week.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I do believe I've truly cracked this "humanitarian management" thing, though Researcher Regulus may disagree.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I would be inclined to disagree as well.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Besides, we've already been back for three weeks now.
Their chatter is cut short as the meeting room door opens. An assistant walks in along with another not-unfamiliar face.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Enough about all that. Settle in, everyone. And would you get down from that table!? The meeting's about to begin.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ahem. Considering some of you never have, or have never, cared to understand Laplace's structure, I think it's necessary I fill you in.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The Funding Committee and the Staff Committee are responsible for evaluating the risk of each project. Put simply, they are the ones who approve or fail your budget applications.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: With that said, allow me to introduce Mr. Ludwig, the new representative of the Staff Committee.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Greetings, everyone.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I wasn't aware you'd recovered. Glad to see you're well, Mr. Ludwig.
The bird-headed man offers a gentle, appreciative nod.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Thank you. I will be assisting you in your research from now on.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: In fact, the topic of this meeting is related to your prior discussion.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Wait, don't tell me you're going to the party?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Ahaha, no, no. Though, if you think I wouldn't spoil the mood, I'd be more than happy to.
The raven sweeps his gaze across the assembled researchers.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I've read the letter from Lorentz Butterfly.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Over the years, Manus Vindictae has never ceased its pursuit of a resurrection ritual.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Many of their actions have caught our attention: searching for the scripts of Renaissance alchemists, taking control of the Fountain of Youth in Bimini—all done after a certain Cavendish descendant joined their ranks.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Tsk. Sounds just like what a mad alchemist would do.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But, given what we know now, they've succeeded at least once.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You're speaking of Antarctica.
The mention of that event draws a long, poignant silence.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: If Lorentz Butterfly can bring us some of this Manus pigment, then there's a chance we can figure out how it works.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Their ritual has brought back a person who doesn't belong to this era. Most would call it a miracle to brave the "Storm" in such a way.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Have we considered that this may also be a means to truly understanding the "Storm"?
The room erupts again.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Brave the "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Mr. Ludwig, have you considered the hypothesis that the "Storm" doesn't cause physical death?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I have. It suggests that those who disappear in the "Storm" are not technically dead.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then where do they go?

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: Over the years, Foundation branches around the world have reported on the reappearance of friends and family, though changed in some way and firmly of the current "Storm" era. It seems these anomalies have become increasingly frequent.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: The Staff Committee is also monitoring these anomalies. We can't afford to overlook any details, no matter how insignificant they may seem.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then we can't just sit here waiting for someone to send a letter when they're in the mood for it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That is, if the Staff Committee allows us to act ...
He lets the words rest before turning to a new topic.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As it happens, after the second letter, I took the initiative to commission someone to investigate.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Though she's a Foundation employee, her body was made by Laplace. So, she volunteered to do some fieldwork for us.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: There may be the occasional "minor incident," but she's in the Timekeeper's unit, so she can be trusted.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: An excellent choice. With the Timekeeper's help, she can operate without the Foundation's surveillance.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Exactly. And she's particularly adept at keeping secrets.

items.speaker: Ludwig
items.text: I hope this won't involve any inhumane methods, Adler.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No need. Her memory will take care of it for us, or should I say, her lack thereof.
Suburb, Mexico City
In the scorching wilderness, a glow of arcane skill flickers.
Enigma's trusted investigator teleports into the place where the flickering light had been.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Uhh, I better double-check the destination. Mexico City, Mexico.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Huh, but this doesn't look like a city.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Was there something wrong with the teleport disk? Defective, I guess? I did hear that Laplace is working on a reusable version.
As she looks out with confusion at the strangeness of her point of arrival, her communicator rings.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Is everything alright, Ms. Latham?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: All good, Mr. Adler. I've arrived in Mexico City.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Please let Madam Lucy know that I'm more than happy to be helping Laplace.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Madam Lucy is no longer at Laplace.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Forget it. We've just received the latest letter.
On the other end, the substitute director drones through its contents.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: These are the possible starting points.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If you encounter Manus Vindictae, avoid confrontation and prioritize your own safety, Ms. Latham.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Don't worry about me. I've borrowed the Rumbling Roaring Box from Mr. Ulrich.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: All I have to do is turn it on, and it'll show me all the places nearby with supernatural stuff going on.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Wait, where's my luggage?
Not far off, she spies a Desert Devil Lizard hauling her belongings away.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Stop right there!
